answer: An agent economy pays each identity only for a distinct, key-sealed replica of a 1 GB ledger shard. Sealing runs per-key, so 1000 clones must store 1000 real gigabytes, never one shared copy. A comet, a recurring audit, reads random byte offsets a yarrow generator derives from the epoch, and a key that misses the window forfeits its 500 POA bond. The nectar flows only to keys answering live, so storage cost grows linearly with n and no farm dedups its way to a cheap seat.
